coverage_claim: Dual-provider research synthesis for a format-independent Lifecycle / Status mixin. It covers governed state machines, concurrent status axes, current assertions, transition history, bitemporal validity, correction, succession, suspension, revocation, end-of-life, operations and external mappings. Domain-specific status vocabularies remain profiles, not universal core codes.

boundary_decision.rationale: Both independent providers model lifecycle semantics as a reusable binding to a host subject or aspect. The host object, executing workflow, version/change history, time reference data, evidence, access policy and disposition schedule retain their own identity and ownership.

add_findings.rationale: Adds first-class identity and mastership for the lifecycle binding itself and explicitly forbids using a date as its identifier.
Makes the host subject, governed aspect and multiplicity of concurrent lifecycle bindings directly answerable.
Adds an explicit family/profile boundary so workflow, publication and clinical interpretation codes are not treated as one universal vocabulary.
Adds the legal active-state set, child-machine sessions and the loss report required when a multi-state configuration is projected to one status code.
Preserves the material distinction among replacement, entered-in-error, retirement and inactivity and the integrity obligation to retain ignored records.

add_functions.rationale: Lifecycle attachment to a specific host aspect is a separate operation from executing a transition.
Error correction must preserve audit integrity and cannot be reduced to ordinary invalidation or deletion.
Hierarchical/parallel state-machine history restoration is a distinct operation with legality and audit requirements.

decisions.concept: Lifecycle / Status is a host-bound mixin
decisions.rationale: A lifecycle binding governs the status of an identified host or aspect without replacing the host or its domain model.

decisions.concept: Five-bundle base plus explicit binding and profile findings
decisions.rationale: Claude provides the stronger boundaries for definition, assertion/history, bitemporality, disposition and operations. Grok adds binding identity, host/aspect multiplicity, profile families, active configuration and entered-in-error semantics.

decisions.concept: One universal canonical status code list
decisions.rationale: Workflow, publication, clinical interpretation, records and other lifecycle families use incompatible meanings. The core defines mapping contracts and patterns, while codes remain versioned profiles.

decisions.concept: One status field represents the whole object
decisions.rationale: A host may carry multiple orthogonal lifecycle bindings and a state machine may have a legal set of concurrent active states. Any scalar projection must declare loss.
Every accepted transition records prior/new configuration, authority, reason, evidence, event time, record time and correction semantics.

decisions.concept: Valid time and transaction time are interchangeable
decisions.rationale: Retroactive correction and reproducible as-of queries require separate valid, event, observation and record times.

decisions.concept: Unknown, inactive, completed, retired, revoked and entered-in-error are synonyms
decisions.rationale: They have different evidence, authority, consumer behavior, reversibility, retention and integrity consequences.

decisions.concept: Timestamp as lifecycle binding or transition identifier
decisions.rationale: Use the master-system identifier or UUIDv7/ULID. RFC 3339 timestamps with seconds and explicit timezone remain separate temporal facts.

decisions.concept: Physical delete is the ordinary terminal transition
decisions.rationale: Retirement, tombstone, erasure and disposition are separately governed; history needed for integrity, signatures, audit or legal retention cannot be silently removed.

publication_holds: Verify live editions and claim-level support for all accepted SCXML, W3C PROV/OWL-Time, HL7 FHIR, DCMI, ISO and records-management sources.
Validate the mixin against at least five independent profiles: publication, workflow/request, clinical interpretation, software release and records disposition.
deferred_research: Formal model checking and executable conformance suites for hierarchical and parallel state machines.
Distributed transition conflict resolution, offline replicas, consensus and eventual-consistency profiles.
Jurisdiction-specific records disposition, legal hold, erasure and evidentiary integrity requirements.
Domain mappings for court cases, security incidents, payments, projects, products, clinical resources and public-sector decisions.
Probabilistic, fuzzy and partially observed state models that do not fit deterministic status assertions.
